{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use the existing Spring XD and Spring Batch extension points wherever possible, preserving backward compatibility for existing XML-based jobs and modules.",
    "Implement Hadoop NameNode configuration through standard Spring properties configuration, with explicit precedence between configured values and command-line or session-level overrides.",
    "Implement the jdbchdfs passthrough mode as a direct reader-to-writer path that bypasses chunk-oriented processing while preserving job status, transaction, restart, and error semantics.",
    "Decouple execution-context creation and restoration from job-launch lifecycle operations using the applicable Spring Batch extension or upgraded release, then remove or refactor the existing XD-2486 workaround.",
    "Support Java Config jobs by discovering and registering job beans from custom module application contexts, while retaining support for XML job definitions.",
    "Define a pluggable execution SPI for Cloud Foundry/Diego-style execution, with the Receptor API implemented as an adapter rather than embedded in core execution logic.",
    "Add shortDescription to the module metadata and documentation model, and expose it consistently in generated and manually maintained module documentation.",
    "For Python scripts stored in HDFS, stage the script to a local temporary file before invoking the shell processor, then capture standard output, standard error, exit status, and cleanup behavior.",
    "Use automated unit and integration tests for each story, with focused regression coverage for job launch, configuration, serialization, HDFS access, and module discovery."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing Spring XD, Spring Batch, Hadoop, and module documentation repositories are available locally and buildable with the current supported toolchain.",
    "The implementation targets Java 17 or a compatible Spring Framework 6/Spring Batch baseline, unless the existing repository requires a directly compatible maintenance version.",
    "One workday represents approximately eight hours of focused development effort; elapsed time for external reviews, upstream releases, or CI queues is excluded.",
    "The developer can modify the relevant Spring Batch integration or consume a locally available Spring Batch change; waiting for an independent upstream release is out of scope.",
    "Existing command-line interfaces, deployment infrastructure, Hadoop cluster access, Cloud Foundry/Diego environment, and Receptor test facilities are available for integration testing.",
    "The wiki migration means moving the existing wiki content into a version-controlled project documentation location, preserving useful links and navigation; major content rewriting is out of scope.",
    "The NameNode configuration applies to the existing DSL session and Hadoop module configuration model; support for multiple independently configured Hadoop clusters is out of scope.",
    "The jdbchdfs passthrough mode applies to the existing batch job type and does not introduce a new general-purpose streaming runtime.",
    "The Java Config custom job requirement concerns discovery, registration, deployment, and launch of a valid custom job module, not a redesign of the entire module packaging system.",
    "The Diego/Lattice work is a functional proof of concept with a stable SPI and one Receptor implementation; production-grade multi-platform orchestration is out of scope.",
    "All module documentation can be updated using existing templates or conventions, without a new documentation portal.",
    "Python execution uses an already available shell processor and Python runtime; implementing Python dependency management, sandboxing, or a remote execution service is out of scope.",
    "Effort includes implementation, developer-authored tests, documentation updates, and local integration verification, but excludes project management and independent formal security review."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository assessment and increment design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing Spring XD, Spring Batch integration, module metadata, DSL configuration, job deployment, HDFS, shell processor, and documentation structures; identify impacted components and define interfaces, compatibility constraints, and test seams for all eight stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Migrate wiki content into the project repository",
      "activity_description": "Move existing wiki pages into version-controlled documentation, preserve or repair internal references, add navigation and contribution guidance, and verify that the repository documentation build or rendering process includes the migrated content.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Add automatic Hadoop NameNode configuration",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration properties and binding for the Hadoop NameNode location, integrate them with DSL session initialization and existing Hadoop clients, define override precedence, provide validation and useful error messages, and add unit and configuration integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Implement jdbchdfs passthrough batch mode",
      "activity_description": "Add a mode that connects the JDBC/HDFS processing path without chunk read/write processing, preserve job lifecycle and failure behavior, expose the mode through the existing job configuration surface, and test normal completion, errors, restart behavior, and compatibility with the existing chunk mode.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Decouple execution context from job launch lifecycle",
      "activity_description": "Apply the required Spring Batch execution-context lifecycle change, update the XD integration to the compatible Batch release or implementation, refactor the XD-2486 workaround, address class-loader and serialization boundaries, and add regression tests for launch, restart, serialization, and context restoration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Support Java Config custom job modules",
      "activity_description": "Update module application-context discovery and job registration so Java Config job beans are detected and deployed, ensure the deployed job is available to the launch command, preserve XML configuration behavior, improve diagnostics for missing jobs, and add end-to-end packaging, deployment, and launch tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Design and implement pluggable Diego execution SPI",
      "activity_description": "Define the platform-neutral execution SPI, lifecycle and status contracts, error handling, and configuration model; implement the Receptor API adapter; integrate it with the XD-on-Lattice/Diego proof of concept; and add mock-based unit tests plus an integration-level execution flow test.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Add shortDescription to module documentation",
      "activity_description": "Extend module metadata and documentation templates to include shortDescription, update all affected module documentation, verify generated or rendered output, and add checks that prevent missing descriptions from silently disappearing.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Support Python scripts hosted in HDFS",
      "activity_description": "Add HDFS script retrieval and local staging to the shell processor path, invoke the Python script with the required arguments and environment, propagate output and exit status back into XD, handle temporary-file cleanup and failures, and test HDFS access, execution, and error cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-story integration, regression testing, and release documentation",
      "activity_description": "Run the full build and regression suite, resolve integration issues among configuration, job lifecycle, module deployment, HDFS, and execution changes, add or update user-facing examples and upgrade notes, and verify packaging and backward compatibility.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 74
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD and Spring Batch extension points wherever possible, preserving backward compatibility for existing XML-based jobs and modules.
Implement Hadoop NameNode configuration through standard Spring properties configuration, with explicit precedence between configured values and command-line or session-level overrides.
Implement the jdbchdfs passthrough mode as a direct reader-to-writer path that bypasses chunk-oriented processing while preserving job status, transaction, restart, and error semantics.

Decouple execution-context creation and restoration from job-launch lifecycle operations using the applicable Spring Batch extension or upgraded release, then remove or refactor the existing XD-2486 workaround.
Support Java Config jobs by discovering and registering job beans from custom module application contexts, while retaining support for XML job definitions.
Define a pluggable execution SPI for Cloud Foundry/Diego-style execution, with the Receptor API implemented as an adapter rather than embedded in core execution logic.
Add shortDescription to the module metadata and documentation model, and expose it consistently in generated and manually maintained module documentation.
For Python scripts stored in HDFS, stage the script to a local temporary file before invoking the shell processor, then capture standard output, standard error, exit status, and cleanup behavior.
Use automated unit and integration tests for each story, with focused regression coverage for job launch, configuration, serialization, HDFS access, and module discovery.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD, Spring Batch, Hadoop, and module documentation repositories are available locally and buildable with the current supported toolchain.
The implementation targets Java 17 or a compatible Spring Framework 6/Spring Batch baseline, unless the existing repository requires a directly compatible maintenance version.
One workday represents approximately eight hours of focused development effort; elapsed time for external reviews, upstream releases, or CI queues is excluded.
The developer can modify the relevant Spring Batch integration or consume a locally available Spring Batch change; waiting for an independent upstream release is out of scope.
Existing command-line interfaces, deployment infrastructure, Hadoop cluster access, Cloud Foundry/Diego environment, and Receptor test facilities are available for integration testing.
The wiki migration means moving the existing wiki content into a version-controlled project documentation location, preserving useful links and navigation; major content rewriting is out of scope.
The NameNode configuration applies to the existing DSL session and Hadoop module configuration model; support for multiple independently configured Hadoop clusters is out of scope.
The jdbchdfs passthrough mode applies to the existing batch job type and does not introduce a new general-purpose streaming runtime.
The Java Config custom job requirement concerns discovery, registration, deployment, and launch of a valid custom job module, not a redesign of the entire module packaging system.
The Diego/Lattice work is a functional proof of concept with a stable SPI and one Receptor implementation; production-grade multi-platform orchestration is out of scope.
All module documentation can be updated using existing templates or conventions, without a new documentation portal.
Python execution uses an already available shell processor and Python runtime; implementing Python dependency management, sandboxing, or a remote execution service is out of scope.
Effort includes implementation, developer-authored tests, documentation updates, and local integration verification, but excludes project management and independent formal security review.
